`useOptionalEntityRoute()` is the only source of URL prefixes; nothing beyond the returned entity's kind, namespace and name reaches the target (FR-16).

`useOptionalEntityRoute()` is private and takes no parameters. Its whole body is a try that returns `useRouteRef(entityRouteRef)` and a catch that returns undefined, the shape of `useRouteResolutionApi` in the style file, with no eslint-disable. A one-line comment says that `useRouteRef` throws on an unresolved ref, and that inside a Router its hooks run in the same order whether or not it throws.

Import `useRouteRef` from `@backstage/core-plugin-api`, never from `@backstage/frontend-plugin-api`. Call `useOptionalEntityRoute()` unconditionally at the top level, after `useNavigate` and `useLocation`, which throw uncaught outside a Router, so the catch only ever sees route failures.

sites.rule: Add `stringifyEntityRef` from `@backstage/catalog-model` as its own import above this one, and add `useRouteRef` to this import.

Declare the private `useOptionalEntityRoute()` above the hook. Keep the hooks and the `!name` effect, and add, after `catalogApi`, `const location = useLocation();` and `const entityRoute = useOptionalEntityRoute();`. The async function of `useAsyncRetry`, with the same deps: (1) await `getEntityByRef`; on a hit return `{ entity }`, so no former lookup runs (NFR-5). (2) When `entityRoute` is undefined return `{}`, so no former lookup runs (FR-27). (3) Put steps 4 to 6 in one try/catch whose catch returns `{}`, so a route function that throws also ends at the not-found page. (4) Await `catalogApi.getEntityByFormerRef?.({ kind, namespace, name })`; on no result return `{}`. (5) Compute `oldPath = entityRoute(entityRouteParams({ kind, namespace, name }, { encodeParams: true }))`. Take `subPath` as `location.pathname.slice(oldPath.length)` when the lowercased pathname starts with the lowercased `oldPath`, else `''`. (6) Return `{ redirect: { to: entityRoute(entityRouteParams(renamed, { encodeParams: true })) + subPath + location.search + location.hash, formerEntityRef: stringifyEntityRef({ kind, namespace, name }) } }`. Add an effect that, when `value?.redirect` is set and its `formerEntityRef` equals the ref of the current params, calls `navigate(redirect.to, { replace: true, state: { formerEntityRef: redirect.formerEntityRef } })`; the ref is computed only inside that branch because `name` can be missing. Return `{ entity: value?.entity, loading: loading || !!value?.redirect, error, refresh }`, so the page stays loading until the new route's lookup replaces the value (FR-18).
